generated_content.presentation_title: A Mountain of Easter Eggs: A Heartwarming Tribute to Harvey

slides.title: A Mountain of Easter Eggs
bullets: A family from Furness Vale, Derbyshire, has been overwhelmed by the response to their Easter egg donation to Sheffield Children's Hospital.
The donation, which started with 72 eggs, has now exceeded 1,000 eggs from kind strangers across the globe.
The eggs are a tribute to the family's late son, Harvey, who passed away last year due to a mystery illness.
slides.speaker_notes: The family, consisting of Lian Marshall and her two daughters, Ellie and Taylor, decided to donate their Easter eggs to the hospital where Harvey was cared for. The response has been overwhelming, with donations coming from as far as the US, Ireland, Scotland, and England.

claim.text: A family from Furness Vale, Derbyshire, has been overwhelmed by the response to their Easter egg donation to Sheffield Children's Hospital.

evidence.chunk_content:
It's every chocoholic's dream come true - a mountain of Easter eggs covering the entire house.

But while Lian Marshall - pictured among the treats - does have two chocolate-loving daughters, this incredible bounty is not for them.

Ellie, 10, and Taylor, five, lost their eight-year-old brother Harvey last year to a mystery illness, and when Easter approached they decided to donate all their eggs to the patients at Sheffield Children's Hospital where he was cared for.

evidence.chunk_content:
Lian Marshall - pictured among the treats - has two chocolate-loving daughters but this incredible bounty is not for them.

Instead the eggs will be donated to Sheffield Children's Hospital .

Once the family, from Furness Vale, Derbyshire, posted on Facebook, kind strangers began to send eggs - and now there are more than 1,000.

Some donations have come from as far afield as the US, with many from Ireland and Scotland and the length and breadth of England.

evidence.chunk_content:
The girls came up with the inspirational idea after spending three Easters in a row by Harvey's side at the hospital where they were all lucky enough to receive Easter Eggs.

Ellie said: 'I thought it was going to be never-ending!

It feels really nice to remember him and I don't think the hospital were expecting as many.

Ellie Marshall, 10, and Taylor Biggin (both above with mother Lian), five, came up with the idea in memory of their brother Harvey .

'It feels a bit strange at the moment.
